title: Circle geometry: what the diagram is telling you
subtitle: A Kuphanda revision guide for MSCE Mathematics

blocks.text: Why the diagram decides the method

In circle geometry the marks are not in the wording, they are in the drawing. Two questions can read almost the same and need completely different theorems, because one diagram shows a diameter and the other does not. Before you write anything, mark the centre, mark every point that touches the circle, and look for a straight line that passes through the centre.

blocks.label: Start here
blocks.text: A line from the centre to a point on the circle is a radius. Every radius has the same length, so any triangle with two radii in it is isosceles — and that alone gives you two equal base angles.
Figure 1: a chord AB with radii OA and OB, and the angle at the centre marked.

figure.alt: Circle centre O with chord AB and radii OA and OB

items: Angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
Angle in a semicircle is 90°, because the arc is the whole half-circle.
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
Angles in the same segment are equal; opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°.

blocks.text: In Figure 1, O is the centre of the circle and A, B and C lie on the circumference. Angle AOB = 2x and angle OAB = x.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why angle OBA is also x.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find angle ACB in terms of x.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Hence find the value of x.

items: OA = OB because both are radii, so triangle AOB is isosceles and the base angles are equal: angle OBA = angle OAB = x.
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc, so angle AOB = 2 × angle ACB, giving angle ACB = x.
Angles of triangle AOB add to 180°: 2x + x + x = 180°, so 4x = 180° and x = 45°.

blocks.text: A tangent touches a circle of radius 9 cm at the point T. P is a point on the tangent such that PT = 12 cm. O is the centre of the circle.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the size of angle OTP, giving a reason.

items: (a) Angle OTP = 90°, because a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
(b) Triangle OTP is right-angled at T, so OP² = OT² + PT² = 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225, and OP = 15 cm.

blocks.text: If you can name the rule before you start calculating, you have usually earned the first mark already. Examiners award it for the reason, not only for the number.
